<document>
<title>Armageddon (1998 film)</title>
<fragment>
*Armageddon* was released on July 1, 1998 in 3,127 theaters in the United States and Canada. It ranked first at the box office ahead of *Dr. Dolittle* with an opening weekend gross of $36 million, combined with $54.2 million from its first five days.[23] Upon opening, the film had the third-highest Fourth of July opening weekend at the time, behind *Men in Black* and *Independence Day*.[24] The film was dethroned by *Lethal Weapon 4* in its second weekend, although it collected a total of $23.5 million.[25] In late July 1998, it surpassed its rival *Deep Impact* to become the highest-grossing domestic release of the year.[26] The film grossed $201.6 million in the United States and Canada and $352.1 million in other territories for a worldwide total of $553.7 million.[2] It was the highest-grossing film of 1998 worldwide and the second-highest-grossing film of that year in the United States, finishing just behind *Saving Private Ryan*.

<document>
<title>Mission: Impossible 2</title>
<fragment>

When *Mission: Impossible 2* first opened, the film was ranked number one at the box office, topping out *Dinosaur*.[29] It held on to the number one spot for two weekends until it was overtaken by *Gone in 60 Seconds*.[30] Around this time, the film went on to become the highest-grossing film of the year domestically, beating *Gladiator*.[31] It would remain so until that December when it was dethroned by *How the Grinch Stole Christmas*.[32] The film eventually grossed $215,409,889 in its North American release and $330,978,216 in other territories for a total worldwide gross of $546,388,105, making this the highest-grossing film of 2000.[4] It is John Woo's highest-grossing film of all time, surpassing *Face/Off*, and was the highest-grossing film in the *Mission: Impossible* series until the release of the fourth film, *Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol*, in 2011.



### Critical response

<document>
<title>Mission: Impossible 2</title>
<fragment>

When *Mission: Impossible 2* first opened, the film was ranked number one at the box office, topping out *Dinosaur*.[29] It held on to the number one spot for two weekends until it was overtaken by *Gone in 60 Seconds*.[30] Around this time, the film went on to become the highest-grossing film of the year domestically, beating *Gladiator*.[31] It would remain so until that December when it was dethroned by *How the Grinch Stole Christmas*.[32] The film eventually grossed $215,409,889 in its North American release and $330,978,216 in other territories for a total worldwide gross of $546,388,105, making this the highest-grossing film of 2000.[4] It is John Woo's highest-grossing film of all time, surpassing *Face/Off*, and was the highest-grossing film in the *Mission: Impossible* series until the release of the fourth film, *Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol*, in 2011.
